newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FORECAST - Brazil Feb trade gap to hit $1.6 billion.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Brazil Feb trade gap to hit $1.6 billion.

text.p: Brazil's trade deficit should reach $1.6 billion in February, with about $600 million of that made up of imports that were not registered in January due to problems with a new import registry, economists said.

"So as not to confuse the issue, we prefer to talk of a January-February deficit of $2.0 billion. The actual defict was about $1.0 billion in each month," said Dany Rappaport, chief economist at MCM Consultores in Brazil.

Brazil officially posted a $413 million trade deficit in January, but the government acknowledged that some $600 million in imports during that month, mostly by state oil firm Petrobras, were not registered.
The Ministry of Industry and Commerce was expected to announce February trade figures on Tuesday.

Last week, ING Barings released a report suggesting the government might have to slow the economy by the middle of the year to squelch import growth. At the current pace of import growth, ING said Brazil's current account deficit would hit an uncomfortable $30 billion in 1997, up from about $24 billion in 1996.
But many economists said Brazil's trade figures, although sobering, were not yet alarming.

"Since the beginning of the year, economists have been talking about a $30 billion current account deficit for 1997. This is not a big deal because it will be fairly easy to finance," said Nilson Teixeira, chief economist for Rio de Janeiro investment bank Fonte-Cindam.
Teixeira said Brazil would avoid balance of payments problems thanks to steady foreign direct investment, which is expected to finance up to half of the nation's current account deficit this year.
Also, some economists are already talking about a brighter trade picture in March.
MCM, which had forecast an $800 million trade gap for March, is planning on cutting that to about $700 million.

"This year's harvests are being sold earlier and it looks like it will be bigger than last year. We are estimating that commodity exports could be $1.0 billion to $1.5 billion more than last year, which is better than previously thought," MCM's Rappaport said.
Brazil posted a $5.5 billion trade deficit in 1996, which is expected to rise to about $8.0 billion this year.
